    84→def _rel_list(s) -> list[str]:
    85→    """Normalize a set or list of paths to sorted relative paths (max 10)."""
    86→    if isinstance(s, set):
    87→        return sorted(rel(x) for x in s)[:10]
    88→    return [rel(x) for x in list(s)[:10]]
    89→
    90→
    91→def _normalize_max_files(value: Any) -> int | None:
    92→    """Normalize max_files input: None/<=0 means unlimited."""
    93→    if value in (None, ""):
    94→        return None
    95→    parsed = int(value)
    96→    return parsed if parsed > 0 else None
    97→
    98→
    99→def _collect_allowed_review_files(
   100→    files: list[str],
   101→    lang: object,
   102→    *,
   103→    base_path: Path | None = None,
   104→) -> set[str]:
   105→    """Return relative production-file paths allowed for holistic review batches."""
   106→    allowed: set[str] = set()
   107→    zone_map = getattr(lang, "zone_map", None)
   108→    resolved_base = base_path.resolve() if isinstance(base_path, Path) else None
   109→    for filepath in files:
   110→        if not isinstance(filepath, str):
   111→            continue
   112→        normalized = filepath.strip().replace("\\", "/")
   113→        if not normalized:
   114→            continue
   115→        if zone_map is not None:
   116→            try:
   117→                zone = zone_map.get(filepath)
   118→                zone_value = getattr(zone, "value", str(zone))
   119→            except (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
   120→                zone_value = "production"
   121→            if zone_value in _NON_PRODUCTION_ZONES:
   122→                continue
   123→        allowed.add(normalized)
   124→        allowed.add(rel(filepath))
   125→        if resolved_base is not None:
   126→            try:
   127→                allowed.add(Path(filepath).resolve().relative_to(resolved_base).as_posix())
   128→            except ValueError as exc:
   129→                _ = exc
   130→    return allowed
   131→
   132→
   133→def _file_in_allowed_scope(filepath: object, allowed_files: set[str]) -> bool:
   134→    """True when *filepath* resolves to a currently in-scope review file."""
   135→    if not isinstance(filepath, str):
   136→        return False
   137→    normalized = filepath.strip().replace("\\", "/")
   138→    if not normalized:
   139→        return False
   140→    if normalized in allowed_files:
   141→        return True
   142→    return rel(filepath) in allowed_files
   143→
   144→
   145→def _filter_issue_focus_to_scope(
   146→    issue_focus: object,
   147→    allowed_files: set[str],
   148→) -> dict[str, object] | None:
   149→    """Drop out-of-scope related_files from historical issue focus payload."""
   150→    if not isinstance(issue_focus, dict):
   151→        return None
   152→    issues_raw = issue_focus.get("issues", [])
   153→    issues: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   154→    if isinstance(issues_raw, list):
   155→        for raw_issue in issues_raw:
   156→            if not isinstance(raw_issue, dict):
   157→                continue
   158→            issue = dict(raw_issue)
   159→            related_raw = issue.get("related_files", [])
   160→            if isinstance(related_raw, list):
   161→                issue["related_files"] = [
   162→                    path
   163→                    for path in related_raw
   164→                    if _file_in_allowed_scope(path, allowed_files)
   165→                ]
   166→            issues.append(issue)
   167→    scoped = dict(issue_focus)
   168→    scoped["issues"] = issues
   169→    scoped["selected_count"] = len(issues)
   170→    return scoped
   171→
   172→
   173→def _filter_batches_to_file_scope(
   174→    batches: list[dict[str, Any]],
   175→    *,
   176→    allowed_files: set[str],
   177→) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
   178→    """Strip out-of-scope files/signals from review batches."""
   179→    if not allowed_files:
   180→        return []
   181→
   182→    scoped_batches: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
   183→    for raw_batch in batches:
   184→        if not isinstance(raw_batch, dict):
   185→            continue
   186→        batch = dict(raw_batch)
   187→        files_to_read = batch.get("files_to_read", [])
   188→        if isinstance(files_to_read, list):
   189→            batch["files_to_read"] = [
   190→                filepath
   191→                for filepath in files_to_read
   192→                if _file_in_allowed_scope(filepath, allowed_files)
   193→            ]
   194→        else:
   195→            batch["files_to_read"] = []
   196→
   197→        concern_signals = batch.get("concern_signals", [])
   198→        if isinstance(concern_signals, list):
   199→            batch["concern_signals"] = [
   200→                signal
   201→                for signal in concern_signals
   202→                if isinstance(signal, dict)
   203→                and _file_in_allowed_scope(signal.get("file", ""), allowed_files)
   204→            ]
   205→            if "concern_signal_count" in batch:
   206→                batch["concern_signal_count"] = len(batch["concern_signals"])
   207→
   208→        issue_focus = _filter_issue_focus_to_scope(
   209→            batch.get("historical_issue_focus"),
   210→            allowed_files,
   211→        )
   212→        if issue_focus is not None:
   213→            batch["historical_issue_focus"] = issue_focus
   214→
   215→        has_seed_files = bool(batch["files_to_read"])
   216→        has_signals = bool(batch.get("concern_signals"))
   217→        if has_seed_files or has_signals:
   218→            scoped_batches.append(batch)
   219→    return scoped_batches
   220→
   221→
   222→def prepare_review(
   223→    path: Path,
   224→    lang: object,
   225→    state: dict,
   226→    options: ReviewPrepareOptions | None = None,
   227→) -> dict[str, object]:
   228→    """Prepare review data for agent consumption. Returns structured dict.
   229→
   230→    If *files* is provided, skip file_finder (avoids redundant filesystem walks
   231→    when the caller already has the file list, e.g. from _setup_lang).
   232→    """
   233→    resolved_options = options or ReviewPrepareOptions()
   234→    resolved_options.max_files = _normalize_max_files(resolved_options.max_files)
   235→    all_files = (
   236→        resolved_options.files
   237→        if resolved_options.files is not None
   238→        else (lang.file_finder(path) if lang.file_finder else [])
   239→    )
   240→
   241→    # Enable file cache for entire prepare operation — context building,
   242→    # file selection, and content extraction all read the same files.
   243→    already_cached = is_file_cache_enabled()
   244→    if not already_cached:
   245→        enable_file_cache()
   246→    try:
   247→        context = build_review_context(path, lang, state, files=all_files)
   248→        selected = select_files_for_review(
   249→            lang,
   250→            path,
   251→            state,
   252→            options=ReviewSelectionOptions(
   253→                max_files=resolved_options.max_files,
   254→                max_age_days=resolved_options.max_age_days,
   255→                force_refresh=resolved_options.force_refresh,
   256→                files=all_files,
   257→            ),
   258→        )
   259→        file_requests = _build_file_requests(selected, lang, state)
   260→    finally:
   261→        if not already_cached:
   262→            disable_file_cache()
   263→
   264→    default_dims, dimension_prompts, system_prompt = load_dimensions_for_lang(lang.name)
   265→    dims = resolve_dimensions(
   266→        cli_dimensions=resolved_options.dimensions,
   267→        config_dimensions=resolved_options.config_dimensions,
   268→        default_dimensions=default_dims,
   269→    )
   270→    lang_guide = get_lang_guidance(lang.name)
   271→    valid_dims = set(dimension_prompts)
   272→    invalid_requested = [
   273→        dim for dim in (resolved_options.dimensions or []) if dim not in valid_dims
   274→    ]
   275→    invalid_config = [
   276→        dim
   277→        for dim in (resolved_options.config_dimensions or [])
   278→        if dim not in valid_dims
   279→    ]
   280→
   281→    return {
   282→        "command": "review",
   283→        "language": lang.name,
   284→        "dimensions": dims,
   285→        "dimension_prompts": {
   286→            d: dimension_prompts[d] for d in dims if d in dimension_prompts
   287→        },
   288→        "lang_guidance": lang_guide,
   289→        "context": serialize_context(context),
   290→        "system_prompt": system_prompt,
   291→        "files": file_requests,
   292→        "total_candidates": len(file_requests),
   293→        "cache_status": {
   294→            "fresh": count_fresh(state, resolved_options.max_age_days),
   295→            "stale": count_stale(state, resolved_options.max_age_days),
   296→            "new": len(file_requests),
   297→        },
   298→        "invalid_dimensions": {
   299→            "requested": invalid_requested,
   300→            "config": invalid_config,
   301→        },
   302→    }
   303→
   304→
   305→def _build_file_requests(files: list[str], lang, state: dict) -> list[dict]:
   306→    """Build per-file review request dicts."""
   307→    file_requests = []
   308→    for filepath in files:
   309→        content = read_file_text(abs_path(filepath))
   310→        if content is None:
   311→            continue
   312→
   313→        rpath = rel(filepath)
   314→        zone = "production"
   315→        if lang.zone_map is not None:
   316→            zone = lang.zone_map.get(filepath).value
   317→
   318→        neighbors: dict
   319→        if lang.dep_graph:
   320→            entry = dep_graph_lookup(lang.dep_graph, filepath)
   321→            imports_raw = entry.get("imports", set())
   322→            importers_raw = entry.get("importers", set())
   323→            importer_count_value = importer_count(entry)
   324→            neighbors = {
   325→                "imports": _rel_list(imports_raw),
   326→                "importers": _rel_list(importers_raw),
   327→                "importer_count": importer_count_value,
   328→            }
   329→        else:
   330→            neighbors = {}
   331→
   332→        file_requests.append(
   333→            {
   334→                "file": rpath,
   335→                "content": content,
   336→                "zone": zone,
   337→                "loc": len(content.splitlines()),
   338→                "neighbors": neighbors,
   339→                "existing_findings": get_file_findings(state, filepath),
   340→            }
   341→        )
   342→    return file_requests
   343→
   344→
   345→def prepare_holistic_review(
   346→    path: Path,
   347→    lang: object,
   348→    state: dict,
   349→    options: HolisticReviewPrepareOptions | None = None,
   350→) -> dict[str, object]:
   351→    """Prepare holistic review data for agent consumption. Returns structured dict."""
   352→    resolved_options = options or HolisticReviewPrepareOptions()
   353→    all_files = (
   354→        resolved_options.files
   355→        if resolved_options.files is not None
   356→        else (lang.file_finder(path) if lang.file_finder else [])
   357→    )
   358→    allowed_review_files = _collect_allowed_review_files(
   359→        all_files,
   360→        lang,
   361→        base_path=path,
   362→    )
   363→
   364→    already_cached = is_file_cache_enabled()
   365→    if not already_cached:
   366→        enable_file_cache()
   367→    try:
   368→        context = HolisticContext.from_raw(
   369→            build_holistic_context(path, lang, state, files=all_files)
   370→        )
   371→        # Also include per-file review context for reference
   372→        review_ctx = build_review_context(path, lang, state, files=all_files)
   373→    finally:
   374→        if not already_cached:
   375→            disable_file_cache()
   376→
   377→    default_dims, holistic_prompts, system_prompt = load_dimensions_for_lang(lang.name)
   378→    _, per_file_prompts, _ = load_dimensions_for_lang(lang.name)
   379→    dims = resolve_dimensions(
   380→        cli_dimensions=resolved_options.dimensions,
   381→        default_dimensions=default_dims,
   382→    )
   383→    lang_guide = get_lang_guidance(lang.name)
   384→    valid_dims = set(holistic_prompts) | set(per_file_prompts)
   385→    invalid_requested = [
   386→        dim for dim in (resolved_options.dimensions or []) if dim not in valid_dims
   387→    ]
   388→    invalid_default = [dim for dim in default_dims if dim not in valid_dims]
   389→    batches = _build_investigation_batches(
   390→        context,
   391→        lang,
   392→        repo_root=path,
   393→        max_files_per_batch=resolved_options.max_files_per_batch,
   394→    )
   395→
   396→    # Append design-coherence batch from mechanical concern signals.
   397→    try:
   398→        from desloppify.engine.concerns import generate_concerns
   399→
   400→        concerns = generate_concerns(state, lang_name=lang.name)
   401→        concerns = [
   402→            concern
   403→            for concern in concerns
   404→            if _file_in_allowed_scope(getattr(concern, "file", ""), allowed_review_files)
   405→        ]
   406→        concerns_batch = _batch_concerns(
   407→            concerns,
   408→            max_files=resolved_options.max_files_per_batch,
   409→            active_dimensions=dims,
   410→        )
   411→        if concerns_batch:
   412→            batches.append(concerns_batch)
   413→    except (ImportError, AttributeError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
   414→        logger.debug("Concern generation failed (best-effort): %s", exc)
   415→
   416→    batches = _filter_batches_to_dimensions(
   417→        batches,
   418→        dims,
   419→        fallback_max_files=resolved_options.max_files_per_batch,
   420→    )
   421→    include_full_sweep = bool(resolved_options.include_full_sweep)
   422→    # Explicitly scoped dimension runs should stay scoped by default.
   423→    if resolved_options.dimensions:
   424→        include_full_sweep = False
   425→    if include_full_sweep:
   426→        append_full_sweep_batch(
   427→            batches=batches,
   428→            dims=dims,
   429→            all_files=all_files,
   430→            lang=lang,
   431→            max_files=resolved_options.max_files_per_batch,
   432→        )
   433→    batches = _filter_batches_to_file_scope(
   434→        batches,
   435→        allowed_files=allowed_review_files,
   436→    )
   437→
   438→    # Holistic mode can receive per-file-oriented dimensions via CLI suggestions.
   439→    # Attach whichever prompt definition exists so reviewers always get guidance.
   440→    selected_prompts: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
   441→    for dim in dims:
   442→        prompt = holistic_prompts.get(dim)
   443→        if prompt is None:
   444→            prompt = per_file_prompts.get(dim)
   445→        if prompt is None:
   446→            continue
   447→        selected_prompts[dim] = prompt
   448→
   449→    payload = {
   450→        "command": "review",
   451→        "mode": "holistic",
   452→        "language": lang.name,
   453→        "dimensions": dims,
   454→        "dimension_prompts": selected_prompts,
   455→        "lang_guidance": lang_guide,
   456→        "holistic_context": context.to_dict(),
   457→        "review_context": serialize_context(review_ctx),
   458→        "system_prompt": system_prompt,
   459→        "total_files": context.codebase_stats.get("total_files", 0),
   460→        "workflow": HOLISTIC_WORKFLOW,
   461→        "investigation_batches": batches,
   462→        "invalid_dimensions": {
   463→            "requested": invalid_requested,
   464→            "default": invalid_default,
   465→        },
   466→    }
   467→    if resolved_options.include_issue_history:
   468→        history_payload = build_issue_history_context(
   469→            state,
   470→            options=ReviewHistoryOptions(
   471→                max_issues=resolved_options.issue_history_max_issues,
   472→            ),
   473→        )
   474→        payload["historical_review_issues"] = history_payload
   475→        for batch in batches:
   476→            if not isinstance(batch, dict):
   477→                continue
   478→            batch_dims = batch.get("dimensions", [])
   479→            batch["historical_issue_focus"] = build_batch_issue_focus(
   480→                history_payload,
   481→                dimensions=batch_dims,
   482→                max_items=resolved_options.issue_history_max_batch_items,
   483→            )
   484→        batches = _filter_batches_to_file_scope(
   485→            batches,
   486→            allowed_files=allowed_review_files,
   487→        )
   488→        payload["investigation_batches"] = batches
   489→    return payload
   490→

    15→def _try_expand_cluster(pattern: str) -> list[str] | None:
    16→    """If pattern matches a cluster name, return its finding IDs."""
    17→    try:
    18→        if not has_living_plan():
    19→            return None
    20→        plan = load_plan()
    21→        cluster = plan.get("clusters", {}).get(pattern)
    22→        if cluster and cluster.get("finding_ids"):
    23→            return list(cluster["finding_ids"])
    24→    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as exc:
    25→        _ = exc
    26→    return None

    29→def _resolve_all_patterns(
    30→    state: dict,
    31→    args: argparse.Namespace,
    32→    *,
    33→    attestation: str | None,
    34→) -> list[str]:
    35→    all_resolved: list[str] = []
    36→    for pattern in args.patterns:
    37→        # Check if pattern is a cluster name — expand to member IDs
    38→        cluster_ids = _try_expand_cluster(pattern)
    39→        if cluster_ids:
    40→            for fid in cluster_ids:
    41→                resolved = state_mod.resolve_findings(
    42→                    state,
    43→                    fid,
    44→                    args.status,
    45→                    args.note,
    46→                    attestation=attestation,
    47→                )
    48→                all_resolved.extend(resolved)
    49→            continue
    50→
    51→        resolved = state_mod.resolve_findings(
    52→            state,
    53→            pattern,
    54→            args.status,
    55→            args.note,
    56→            attestation=attestation,
    57→        )
    58→        all_resolved.extend(resolved)
    59→    return all_resolved

     5→from copy import deepcopy
     6→
     7→__all__ = [
     8→    "suppression_metrics",
     9→]
    10→
    11→from desloppify.core._internal.coercions import coerce_confidence
    12→from desloppify.core.enums import finding_status_tokens
    13→from desloppify.engine._scoring.policy.core import matches_target_score
    14→from desloppify.engine._state.filtering import path_scoped_findings
    15→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import StateModel, ensure_state_defaults
    16→from desloppify.languages._framework.base.types import ScanCoverageRecord
    17→
    18→_EMPTY_COUNTERS = tuple(sorted(finding_status_tokens()))
    19→_SUBJECTIVE_TARGET_RESET_THRESHOLD = 2
    20→
    21→
    22→def _resolve_lang_from_state(state: StateModel) -> str | None:
    23→    """Best-effort language detection from state (scan_history > lang_capabilities)."""
    24→    history = state.get("scan_history")
    25→    if isinstance(history, list):
    26→        for entry in reversed(history):
    27→            if isinstance(entry, dict):
    28→                lang = entry.get("lang")
    29→                if isinstance(lang, str) and lang.strip():
    30→                    return lang.strip().lower()
    31→    capabilities = state.get("lang_capabilities")
    32→    if isinstance(capabilities, dict) and len(capabilities) == 1:
    33→        only_lang = next(iter(capabilities.keys()))
    34→        if isinstance(only_lang, str) and only_lang.strip():
    35→            return only_lang.strip().lower()
    36→    return None
    37→
    38→
    39→def _count_findings(findings: dict) -> tuple[dict[str, int], dict[int, dict[str, int]]]:
    40→    """Tally per-status counters and per-tier breakdowns."""
    41→    counters = dict.fromkeys(_EMPTY_COUNTERS, 0)
    42→    tier_stats: dict[int, dict[str, int]] = {}
    43→
    44→    for finding in findings.values():
    45→        if finding.get("suppressed"):
    46→            continue
    47→        status = finding["status"]
    48→        tier = finding.get("tier", 3)
    49→        counters[status] = counters.get(status, 0) + 1
    50→        tier_counter = tier_stats.setdefault(tier, dict.fromkeys(_EMPTY_COUNTERS, 0))
    51→        tier_counter[status] = tier_counter.get(status, 0) + 1
    52→
    53→    return counters, tier_stats
    54→
    55→
    56→def _coerce_subjective_score(value: dict | float | int | str | None) -> float:
    57→    """Normalize a subjective assessment score payload to a 0-100 float."""
    58→    raw = value.get("score", 0) if isinstance(value, dict) else value
    59→    try:
    60→        score = float(raw)
    61→    except (TypeError, ValueError):
    62→        score = 0.0
    63→    return max(0.0, min(100.0, score))
    64→
    65→
    66→def _subjective_target_matches(
    67→    subjective_assessments: dict, *, target: float
    68→) -> list[str]:
    69→    """Return dimension keys whose subjective score matches the target band."""
    70→    matches = [
    71→        dimension
    72→        for dimension, payload in subjective_assessments.items()
    73→        if matches_target_score(_coerce_subjective_score(payload), target)
    74→    ]
    75→    return sorted(matches)
    76→
    77→
    78→def _subjective_integrity_baseline(target: float | None) -> dict[str, object]:
    79→    """Create baseline subjective-integrity metadata for scan/reporting output."""
    80→    return {
    81→        "status": "disabled" if target is None else "pass",
    82→        "target_score": None if target is None else round(float(target), 2),
    83→        "matched_count": 0,
    84→        "matched_dimensions": [],
    85→        "reset_dimensions": [],
    86→    }
    87→
    88→
    89→def _apply_subjective_integrity_policy(
    90→    subjective_assessments: dict,
    91→    *,
    92→    target: float,
    93→) -> tuple[dict, dict[str, object]]:
    94→    """Apply anti-gaming penalties for subjective scores clustered on the target."""
    95→    normalized_target = max(0.0, min(100.0, float(target)))
    96→    matched_dimensions = _subjective_target_matches(
    97→        subjective_assessments,
    98→        target=normalized_target,
    99→    )
   100→    meta = _subjective_integrity_baseline(normalized_target)
   101→    meta["matched_count"] = len(matched_dimensions)
   102→    meta["matched_dimensions"] = matched_dimensions
   103→
   104→    if len(matched_dimensions) < _SUBJECTIVE_TARGET_RESET_THRESHOLD:
   105→        meta["status"] = "warn" if matched_dimensions else "pass"
   106→        return subjective_assessments, meta
   107→
   108→    adjusted = deepcopy(subjective_assessments)
   109→    for dimension in matched_dimensions:
   110→        payload = adjusted.get(dimension)
   111→        if isinstance(payload, dict):
   112→            payload["score"] = 0.0
   113→            payload["integrity_penalty"] = "target_match_reset"
   114→        else:
   115→            adjusted[dimension] = {
   116→                "score": 0.0,
   117→                "integrity_penalty": "target_match_reset",
   118→            }
   119→
   120→    meta["status"] = "penalized"
   121→    meta["reset_dimensions"] = matched_dimensions
   122→    return adjusted, meta
   123→
   124→
   125→def _aggregate_scores(
   126→    dim_scores: dict, compute_health_score_fn
   127→) -> dict[str, float]:
   128→    """Derive the 4 aggregate scores from dimension-level data."""
   129→    mechanical = {
   130→        n: d
   131→        for n, d in dim_scores.items()
   132→        if "subjective_assessment" not in d.get("detectors", {})
   133→    }
   134→    return {
   135→        "overall_score": compute_health_score_fn(dim_scores),
   136→        "strict_score": compute_health_score_fn(
   137→            dim_scores, score_key="strict_score"
   138→        ),
   139→        "objective_score": compute_health_score_fn(mechanical),
   140→        "verified_strict_score": compute_health_score_fn(
   141→            mechanical, [REDACTED]
   142→        ),
   143→    }
   144→

   146→def _active_scan_coverage(state: StateModel) -> ScanCoverageRecord:
   147→    scan_coverage = state.get("scan_coverage", {})
   148→    if not isinstance(scan_coverage, dict) or not scan_coverage:
   149→        return {}
   150→
   151→    lang_name = state.get("lang")
   152→    if isinstance(lang_name, str) and lang_name:
   153→        payload = scan_coverage.get(lang_name, {})
   154→        return payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else {}
   155→
   156→    if len(scan_coverage) == 1:
   157→        only = next(iter(scan_coverage.values()))
   158→        return only if isinstance(only, dict) else {}
   159→    return {}
   160→
   161→
   162→def _apply_scan_coverage_to_dimension_scores(
   163→    state: StateModel,
   164→    *,
   165→    dimension_scores: dict[str, dict],
   166→) -> None:
   167→    coverage_payload = _active_scan_coverage(state)
   168→    detectors_payload = coverage_payload.get("detectors", {})
   169→    if not isinstance(detectors_payload, dict):
   170→        state["score_confidence"] = {
   171→            "status": "full",
   172→            "confidence": 1.0,
   173→            "detectors": [],
   174→            "dimensions": [],
   175→        }
   176→        return
   177→
   178→    reduced_detectors: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
   179→    for detector, raw in detectors_payload.items():
   180→        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
   181→            continue
   182→        status = str(raw.get("status", "full")).lower()
   183→        confidence = coerce_confidence(raw.get("confidence"), default=1.0)
   184→        if status != "reduced" and confidence >= 1.0:
   185→            continue
   186→        reduced_detectors[str(detector)] = dict(raw)
   187→
   188→    reduced_dimensions: list[str] = []
   189→    score_confidence_detectors: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   190→    for detector, payload in reduced_detectors.items():
   191→        score_confidence_detectors.append(
   192→            {
   193→                "detector": detector,
   194→                "status": str(payload.get("status", "reduced")),
   195→                "confidence": round(
   196→                    coerce_confidence(payload.get("confidence"), default=1.0), 2
   197→                ),
   198→                "summary": str(payload.get("summary", "") or ""),
   199→                "impact": str(payload.get("impact", "") or ""),
   200→                "remediation": str(payload.get("remediation", "") or ""),
   201→                "tool": str(payload.get("tool", "") or ""),
   202→                "reason": str(payload.get("reason", "") or ""),
   203→            }
   204→        )
   205→
   206→    for dim_name, dim_data in dimension_scores.items():
   207→        if not isinstance(dim_data, dict):
   208→            continue
   209→        detectors = dim_data.get("detectors", {})
   210→        if not isinstance(detectors, dict):
   211→            continue
   212→
   213→        impacts: list[dict[str, object]] = []
   214→        for detector_name, detector_meta in detectors.items():
   215→            reduced = reduced_detectors.get(str(detector_name))
   216→            if not isinstance(detector_meta, dict):
   217→                continue
   218→            if reduced is None:
   219→                detector_meta.pop("coverage_status", None)
   220→                detector_meta.pop("coverage_confidence", None)
   221→                detector_meta.pop("coverage_summary", None)
   222→                continue
   223→            confidence = coerce_confidence(reduced.get("confidence"), default=1.0)
   224→            status = str(reduced.get("status", "reduced"))
   225→            summary = str(reduced.get("summary", "") or "")
   226→            detector_meta["coverage_status"] = status
   227→            detector_meta["coverage_confidence"] = round(confidence, 2)
   228→            detector_meta["coverage_summary"] = summary
   229→            impacts.append(
   230→                {
   231→                    "detector": str(detector_name),
   232→                    "status": status,
   233→                    "confidence": round(confidence, 2),
   234→                    "summary": summary,
   235→                }
   236→            )
   237→
   238→        if not impacts:
   239→            dim_data.pop("coverage_status", None)
   240→            dim_data.pop("coverage_confidence", None)
   241→            dim_data.pop("coverage_impacts", None)
   242→            continue
   243→
   244→        reduced_dimensions.append(str(dim_name))
   245→        dim_data["coverage_status"] = "reduced"
   246→        dim_data["coverage_confidence"] = round(
   247→            min(coerce_confidence(item.get("confidence"), default=1.0) for item in impacts),
   248→            2,
   249→        )
   250→        dim_data["coverage_impacts"] = impacts
   251→
   252→    if not score_confidence_detectors:
   253→        state["score_confidence"] = {
   254→            "status": "full",
   255→            "confidence": 1.0,
   256→            "detectors": [],
   257→            "dimensions": [],
   258→        }
   259→        return
   260→
   261→    state["score_confidence"] = {
   262→        "status": "reduced",
   263→        "confidence": round(
   264→            min(
   265→                coerce_confidence(item.get("confidence"), default=1.0)
   266→                for item in score_confidence_detectors
   267→            ),
   268→            2,
   269→        ),
   270→        "detectors": score_confidence_detectors,
   271→        "dimensions": sorted(set(reduced_dimensions)),
   272→    }
   273→
   274→
   275→def _update_objective_health(
   276→    state: StateModel,
   277→    findings: dict,
   278→    *,
   279→    subjective_integrity_target: float | None = None,
   280→) -> None:
   281→    """Compute canonical score trio from dimension scoring."""
   282→    pots = state.get("potentials", {})
   283→    if not pots:
   284→        return
   285→
   286→    # Deferred import to avoid circular dependency with desloppify.scoring
   287→    # (scoring -> _scoring/results/core -> _scoring/subjective/core -> review -> state -> _state/merge -> _state/scoring)
   288→    from desloppify.scoring import (
   289→        compute_health_score,
   290→        compute_score_bundle,
   291→        merge_potentials,
   292→    )
   293→
   294→    merged = merge_potentials(pots)
   295→    if not merged:
   296→        return
   297→
   298→    subjective_assessments = state.get("subjective_assessments") or None
   299→    integrity_target = (
   300→        max(0.0, min(100.0, float(subjective_integrity_target)))
   301→        if isinstance(subjective_integrity_target, int | float)
   302→        else None
   303→    )
   304→    integrity_meta = _subjective_integrity_baseline(integrity_target)
   305→    if subjective_assessments and integrity_target is not None:
   306→        subjective_assessments, integrity_meta = _apply_subjective_integrity_policy(
   307→            subjective_assessments,
   308→            target=integrity_target,
   309→        )
   310→    state["subjective_integrity"] = integrity_meta
   311→
   312→    has_active_checks = any((count or 0) > 0 for count in merged.values())
   313→    if not has_active_checks and not subjective_assessments:
   314→        state["dimension_scores"] = {}
   315→        state["overall_score"] = 100.0
   316→        state["objective_score"] = 100.0
   317→        state["strict_score"] = 100.0
   318→        state["verified_strict_score"] = 100.0
   319→        return
   320→
   321→    # Use the full scorecard dimensions for 0-score placeholders so every
   322→    # dimension the review workflow covers gets a placeholder when unreviewed.
   323→    # Explicit assessments outside this set still count
   324→    # (append_subjective_dimensions handles that).
   325→    allowed_subjective: set[str] | None = None
   326→    lang_name = _resolve_lang_from_state(state)
   327→    if lang_name:
   328→        try:
   329→            from desloppify.intelligence.review.dimensions.data import (
   330→                load_dimensions_for_lang,
   331→            )
   332→
   333→            dims, _, _ = load_dimensions_for_lang(lang_name)
   334→            if dims:
   335→                allowed_subjective = set(dims)
   336→        except (ImportError, AttributeError) as exc:
   337→            _ = exc
   338→
   339→    bundle = compute_score_bundle(
   340→        findings,
   341→        merged,
   342→        subjective_assessments=subjective_assessments,
   343→        allowed_subjective_dimensions=allowed_subjective,
   344→    )
   345→    lenient_scores = bundle.dimension_scores
   346→    strict_scores = bundle.strict_dimension_scores
   347→    verified_strict_scores = bundle.verified_strict_dimension_scores
   348→
   349→    prev_dim_scores = dict(state.get("dimension_scores", {}))
   350→
   351→    state["dimension_scores"] = {
   352→        name: dict(
   353→            score=lenient_scores[name]["score"],
   354→            strict_score=strict_scores[name]["score"],
   355→            verified_strict_score=verified_strict_scores[name]["score"],
   356→            checks=lenient_scores[name]["checks"],
   357→            issues=lenient_scores[name]["issues"],
   358→            tier=lenient_scores[name]["tier"],
   359→            detectors=lenient_scores[name].get("detectors", {}),
   360→        )
   361→        for name in lenient_scores
   362→    }
   363→    for data in state["dimension_scores"].values():
   364→        data["strict"] = data["strict_score"]
   365→
   366→    # Carry forward mechanical dimensions from a prior scan that are absent
   367→    # now (e.g. duplication when --skip-slow is used).
   368→    for dim_name, prev_data in prev_dim_scores.items():
   369→        if dim_name in state["dimension_scores"]:
   370→            continue
   371→        if not isinstance(prev_data, dict):
   372→            continue
   373→        if "subjective_assessment" in prev_data.get("detectors", {}):
   374→            continue
   375→        carried = {**prev_data, "carried_forward": True}
   376→        # Backfill for state files written before verified_strict_score existed.
   377→        carried.setdefault(
   378→            "verified_strict_score",
   379→            carried.get("strict_score", carried.get("strict", carried.get("score", 0.0))),
   380→        )
   381→        state["dimension_scores"][dim_name] = carried
   382→
   383→    _apply_scan_coverage_to_dimension_scores(
   384→        state,
   385→        dimension_scores=state["dimension_scores"],
   386→    )
   387→
   388→    state.update(_aggregate_scores(state["dimension_scores"], compute_health_score))
   389→
   390→
   391→def _recompute_stats(
   392→    state: StateModel,
   393→    scan_path: str | None = None,
   394→    *,
   395→    subjective_integrity_target: float | None = None,
   396→) -> None:
   397→    """Recompute stats and canonical health scores from findings."""
   398→    ensure_state_defaults(state)
   399→    findings = path_scoped_findings(state["findings"], scan_path)
   400→    counters, tier_stats = _count_findings(findings)
   401→    state["stats"] = {
   402→        "total": sum(counters.values()),
   403→        **counters,
   404→        "by_tier": {
   405→            str(tier): tier_counts for tier, tier_counts in sorted(tier_stats.items())
   406→        },
   407→    }
   408→    _update_objective_health(
   409→        state,
   410→        findings,
   411→        subjective_integrity_target=subjective_integrity_target,
   412→    )
   413→
   414→
   415→def _empty_suppression_metrics() -> dict[str, int | float]:
   416→    return {
   417→        "last_ignored": 0,
   418→        "last_raw_findings": 0,
   419→        "last_suppressed_pct": 0.0,
   420→        "last_ignore_patterns": 0,
   421→        "recent_scans": 0,
   422→        "recent_ignored": 0,
   423→        "recent_raw_findings": 0,
   424→        "recent_suppressed_pct": 0.0,
   425→    }
   426→
   427→
   428→def suppression_metrics(state: StateModel, *, window: int = 5) -> dict[str, int | float]:
   429→    """Summarize ignore suppression from recent scan history."""
   430→    history = state.get("scan_history", [])
   431→    if not history:
   432→        return _empty_suppression_metrics()
   433→
   434→    scans_with_suppression = [
   435→        entry
   436→        for entry in history
   437→        if isinstance(entry, dict)
   438→        and (
   439→            "ignored" in entry
   440→            or "raw_findings" in entry
   441→            or "suppressed_pct" in entry
   442→            or "ignore_patterns" in entry
   443→        )
   444→    ]
   445→    if not scans_with_suppression:
   446→        return _empty_suppression_metrics()
   447→
   448→    recent = scans_with_suppression[-max(1, window) :]
   449→    last = recent[-1]
   450→
   451→    recent_ignored = sum(int(entry.get("ignored", 0) or 0) for entry in recent)
   452→    recent_raw = sum(int(entry.get("raw_findings", 0) or 0) for entry in recent)
   453→    recent_pct = round(recent_ignored / recent_raw * 100, 1) if recent_raw else 0.0
   454→
   455→    last_ignored = int(last.get("ignored", 0) or 0)
   456→    last_raw = int(last.get("raw_findings", 0) or 0)
   457→    if "suppressed_pct" in last:
   458→        last_pct = round(float(last.get("suppressed_pct") or 0.0), 1)
   459→    else:
   460→        last_pct = round(last_ignored / last_raw * 100, 1) if last_raw else 0.0
   461→
   462→    return {
   463→        "last_ignored": last_ignored,
   464→        "last_raw_findings": last_raw,
   465→        "last_suppressed_pct": last_pct,
   466→        "last_ignore_patterns": int(last.get("ignore_patterns", 0) or 0),
   467→        "recent_scans": len(recent),
   468→        "recent_ignored": recent_ignored,
   469→        "recent_raw_findings": recent_raw,
   470→        "recent_suppressed_pct": recent_pct,
   471→    }
   472→

    89→    failure_set: frozenset[str],
    90→    allowed_dimensions: set[str] | None = None,
    91→) -> None:
    92→    """Append subjective review dimensions to results dict (mutates results).
    93→
    94→    Subjective scoring is evidence-first: open review findings for a dimension
    95→    determine pass-rate, while imported assessment scores are retained as
    96→    metadata for transparency.
    97→    """
    98→    # Deferred import to avoid circular (see _dimension_display_name).
    99→    from desloppify.intelligence.review.dimensions.holistic import DIMENSIONS
   100→
   101→    raw_defaults = DIMENSIONS
   102→    allowed = (
   103→        {_normalize_dimension_key(name) for name in allowed_dimensions}
   104→        if allowed_dimensions is not None
   105→        else None
   106→    )
   107→
   108→    default_dimensions = []
   109→    for raw_dim in raw_defaults:
   110→        dim = _normalize_dimension_key(raw_dim)
   111→        if not dim:
   112→            continue
   113→        if allowed is not None and dim not in allowed:
   114→            continue
   115→        default_dimensions.append(dim)
   116→
   117→    assessed: dict[str, dict] = {}
   118→    for raw_dim, payload in (assessments or {}).items():
   119→        dim = _normalize_dimension_key(raw_dim)
   120→        if not dim:
   121→            continue
   122→        # Real assessments (from review imports) always count regardless of
   123→        # allowed_dimensions — they were deliberately imported and should not
   124→        # be silently discarded.  However, system-generated placeholders
   125→        # (scan_reset_subjective) are not real assessments and should respect
   126→        # the allowed_dimensions scope like defaults.
   127→        is_placeholder = isinstance(payload, dict) and (
   128→            payload.get("placeholder") is True
   129→            or payload.get("source") == "scan_reset_subjective"
   130→            or payload.get("reset_by") == "scan_reset_subjective"
   131→        )
   132→        if is_placeholder and allowed is not None and dim not in allowed:
   133→            continue
   134→        assessed[dim] = payload
   135→    existing_lower = {k.lower() for k in results}
   136→    lang_name = _primary_lang_from_findings(findings)
   137→
   138→    all_dims = list(default_dimensions)
   139→    for dim_name in assessed:
   140→        if dim_name not in default_dimensions:
   141→            all_dims.append(dim_name)
   142→
   143→    for dim_name in all_dims:
   144→        is_default = dim_name in default_dimensions
   145→        assessment = assessed.get(dim_name)
   146→        has_assessment = isinstance(assessment, dict)
   147→        if not is_default and not assessment:
   148→            continue
   149→
   150→        display = _dimension_display_name(dim_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   151→        if display.lower() in existing_lower:
   152→            display = f"{display} (subjective)"
   153→
   154→        # Count open review/concern findings for display (work queue), but
   155→        # these do NOT drive the dimension score — only assessment scores do.
   156→        issue_count = sum(
   157→            1
   158→            for finding in findings.values()
   159→            if finding.get("detector") in ("review", "concerns")
   160→            and finding.get("status") in failure_set
   161→            and _normalize_dimension_key(
   162→                finding.get("detail", {}).get("dimension")
   163→            )
   164→            == dim_name
   165→        )
   166→
   167→        assessment_score = (
   168→            max(0.0, min(100.0, float(assessment.get("score", 0))))
   169→            if isinstance(assessment, dict)
   170→            else 0.0
   171→        )
   172→        integrity_penalty = (
   173→            assessment.get("integrity_penalty")
   174→            if isinstance(assessment, dict)
   175→            else None
   176→        )
   177→        reset_pending = bool(
   178→            isinstance(assessment, dict)
   179→            and (
   180→                assessment.get("reset_by") == "scan_reset_subjective"
   181→                or assessment.get("source") == "scan_reset_subjective"
   182→                or assessment.get("placeholder") is True
   183→            )
   184→        )
   185→        if reset_pending:
   186→            score = 0.0
   187→            pass_rate = 0.0
   188→        elif integrity_penalty == "target_match_reset":
   189→            score = 0.0
   190→            pass_rate = 0.0
   191→        elif has_assessment:
   192→            # Assessment score drives the dimension score directly.
   193→            # Resolving review findings does NOT change this score —
   194→            # only a fresh review import updates it.
   195→            score = assessment_score
   196→            pass_rate = score / 100.0
   197→        else:
   198→            # No assessment yet: explicit unassessed placeholder.
   199→            # Subjective dimensions start at 0 until an assessment is imported.
   200→            score = 0.0
   201→            pass_rate = 0.0
   202→        components: list[str] = []
   203→        component_scores: dict[str, float] = {}
   204→        if isinstance(assessment, dict):
   205→            raw_components = assessment.get("components")
   206→            if isinstance(raw_components, list):
   207→                components = [
   208→                    str(item).strip()
   209→                    for item in raw_components
   210→                    if isinstance(item, str) and item.strip()
   211→                ]
   212→            raw_component_scores = assessment.get("component_scores")
   213→            if isinstance(raw_component_scores, dict):
   214→                for key, value in raw_component_scores.items():
   215→                    if not isinstance(key, str) or not key.strip():
   216→                        continue
   217→                    if not is_numeric(value):
   218→                        continue
   219→                    component_scores[key.strip()] = round(
   220→                        max(0.0, min(100.0, float(value))),
   221→                        1,
   222→                    )
   223→
   224→        results[display] = {
   225→            "score": round(float(score), 1),
   226→            "tier": 4,
   227→            "checks": SUBJECTIVE_CHECKS,
   228→            "issues": issue_count,
   229→            "detectors": {
   230→                "subjective_assessment": {
   231→                    "potential": SUBJECTIVE_CHECKS,
   232→                    "pass_rate": round(pass_rate, 4),
   233→                    "issues": issue_count,
   234→                    "weighted_failures": round(SUBJECTIVE_CHECKS * (1 - pass_rate), 4),
   235→                    "assessment_score": round(assessment_score, 1),
   236→                    "placeholder": reset_pending or not has_assessment,
   237→                    "dimension_key": dim_name,
   238→                    "configured_weight": round(
   239→                        _dimension_weight(dim_name, lang_name=lang_name), 6
   240→                    ),
   241→                    "components": components,
   242→                    **(
   243→                        {"component_scores": component_scores}
   244→                        if component_scores
   245→                        else {}
   246→                    ),
   247→                }
   248→            },
   249→        }
   250→
   251→
   252→__all__ = [
   253→    "DISPLAY_NAMES",
   254→    "append_subjective_dimensions",
   255→]

1→"""Runtime context helpers for command handlers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from dataclasses import dataclass
     6→from pathlib import Path
     7→from typing import Any
     8→
     9→from desloppify import state as state_mod
    10→from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.state import state_path
    11→from desloppify.core.config import load_config
    12→
    13→
    14→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    15→class CommandRuntime:
    16→    """Explicit runtime dependencies shared by command handlers."""
    17→
    18→    config: dict[str, Any]
    19→    state: dict[str, Any]
    20→    state_path: Path | None
    21→
    22→
    23→def command_runtime(args) -> CommandRuntime:
    24→    """Return runtime context from explicit args.runtime or construct one."""
    25→    runtime = getattr(args, "runtime", None)
    26→    if isinstance(runtime, CommandRuntime):
    27→        return runtime
    28→
    29→    config = load_config()
    30→    state_file = state_path(args)
    31→    if isinstance(state_file, str):
    32→        state_file = Path(state_file)
    33→
    34→    state = state_mod.load_state(state_file)
    35→
    36→    return CommandRuntime(config=config, state=state, state_path=state_file)
    37→
    38→
    39→__all__ = ["CommandRuntime", "command_runtime"]
    40→

    35→def _print_plan_agent_block(plan: dict, *, header: str = "  AGENT PLAN:") -> None:
    36→    """Render the living plan as the agent plan block."""

1→"""Target-score normalization helpers for command modules."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.core._internal.text_utils import is_numeric
     6→
     7→
     8→def coerce_target_score(value: object, *, fallback: float = 95.0) -> float:
     9→    """Normalize target score-like values to a safe [0, 100] float."""
    10→    if is_numeric(fallback):
    11→        fallback_value = float(fallback)
    12→    else:
    13→        fallback_value = 95.0
    14→
    15→    if is_numeric(value):
    16→        parsed = float(value)
    17→    elif isinstance(value, str):
    18→        text = value.strip()
    19→        if not text:
    20→            parsed = fallback_value
    21→        else:
    22→            try:
    23→                parsed = float(text)
    24→            except ValueError:
    25→                parsed = fallback_value
    26→    else:
    27→        parsed = fallback_value
    28→    return max(0.0, min(100.0, parsed))
    29→
    30→
    31→def target_strict_score_from_config(
    32→    config: dict | None, *, fallback: float = 95.0
    33→) -> float:
    34→    """Read and normalize target strict score from config."""
    35→    if isinstance(config, dict):
    36→        raw = config.get("target_strict_score", fallback)
    37→    else:
    38→        raw = fallback
    39→    return coerce_target_score(raw, fallback=fallback)

1→"""Language-resolution helpers for command modules."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import logging
     6→from collections.abc import Callable
     7→from functools import lru_cache
     8→from pathlib import Path
     9→from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
    10→
    11→from desloppify import languages as lang_api
    12→from desloppify.core._internal.text_utils import PROJECT_ROOT
    13→
    14→if TYPE_CHECKING:
    15→    from desloppify.languages._framework.base.types import LangConfig
    16→
    17→
    18→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    19→
    20→
    21→class LangResolutionError(SystemExit):
    22→    """Raised when language resolution fails with a user-facing message.
    23→
    24→    Inherits from SystemExit so that callers which don't catch it explicitly
    25→    will still terminate with a non-zero exit code, matching the previous
    26→    sys.exit(1) behaviour.  The CLI top-level catches it to print a clean
    27→    error without a traceback.
    28→    """
    29→
    30→    def __init__(self, message: str) -> None:
    31→        self.message = message
    32→        super().__init__(1)
    33→
    34→
    35→EXTRA_ROOT_MARKERS = (
    36→    "package.json",
    37→    "pyproject.toml",
    38→    "setup.py",
    39→    "setup.cfg",
    40→    "go.mod",
    41→    "Cargo.toml",
    42→)
    43→
    44→
    45→def _cache_once(fn: Callable[[], tuple[str, ...]]) -> Callable[[], tuple[str, ...]]:
    46→    """Cache a zero-arg function once while preserving cache_clear for tests."""
    47→    cached = lru_cache(maxsize=1)(fn)
    48→    return cached
    49→
    50→
    51→@_cache_once
    52→def _lang_config_markers() -> tuple[str, ...]:
    53→    """Collect project-root marker files from language plugins + fallback markers."""
    54→    markers = set(EXTRA_ROOT_MARKERS)
    55→
    56→    for lang_name in lang_api.available_langs():
    57→        try:
    58→            cfg = lang_api.get_lang(lang_name)
    59→        except (ImportError, ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError) as exc:
    60→            logger.debug(
    61→                "Skipping language marker collection for %s: %s", lang_name, exc
    62→            )
    63→            continue
    64→        for marker in getattr(cfg, "detect_markers", []) or []:
    65→            if not isinstance(marker, str):
    66→                continue
    67→            cleaned = marker.strip()
    68→            if cleaned:
    69→                markers.add(cleaned)
    70→    return tuple(sorted(markers))
    71→
    72→
    73→def resolve_detection_root(
    74→    args,
    75→    *,
    76→    project_root: Path = PROJECT_ROOT,
    77→    marker_provider: Callable[[], tuple[str, ...]] | None = None,
    78→) -> Path:
    79→    """Best root to auto-detect language from."""
    80→    marker_provider = marker_provider or _lang_config_markers
    81→    markers = marker_provider()
    82→
    83→    raw_path = getattr(args, "path", None)
    84→    if not raw_path:
    85→        return project_root
    86→
    87→    candidate = Path(raw_path)
    88→    if not candidate.is_absolute():
    89→        candidate = project_root / candidate
    90→    candidate = candidate.resolve()
    91→    search_root = candidate if candidate.is_dir() else candidate.parent
    92→
    93→    for root in (search_root, *search_root.parents):
    94→        if any((root / marker).exists() for marker in markers):
    95→            return root
    96→    return search_root
    97→
    98→
    99→def auto_detect_lang_name(args) -> str | None:
   100→    """Auto-detect language using the most relevant root for this command."""
   101→    root = resolve_detection_root(args)
   102→    detected = lang_api.auto_detect_lang(root)
   103→    if detected is None and root != PROJECT_ROOT:
   104→        detected = lang_api.auto_detect_lang(PROJECT_ROOT)
   105→    return detected
   106→
   107→
   108→def resolve_lang(args) -> LangConfig | None:
   109→    """Resolve language config from args, with auto-detection fallback."""
   110→    lang_name = getattr(args, "lang", None)
   111→    if lang_name is None:
   112→        lang_name = auto_detect_lang_name(args)
   113→    if lang_name is None:
   114→        return None
   115→    try:
   116→        return lang_api.get_lang(lang_name)
   117→    except ValueError as exc:
   118→        langs = lang_api.available_langs()
   119→        langs_str = ", ".join(langs) if langs else "registered language plugins"
   120→        raise LangResolutionError(
   121→            f"{exc}\n  Hint: use --lang to select manually (available: {langs_str})"
   122→        ) from exc
   123→
   124→
   125→def resolve_lang_settings(config: dict, lang: LangConfig) -> dict[str, object]:
   126→    """Resolve persisted per-language settings from config.languages.<lang>."""
   127→    if not isinstance(config, dict):
   128→        return lang.normalize_settings({})
   129→    languages = config.get("languages", {})
   130→    if not isinstance(languages, dict):
   131→        return lang.normalize_settings({})
   132→    raw = languages.get(lang.name, {})
   133→    return lang.normalize_settings(raw if isinstance(raw, dict) else {})
   134→

    23→
    24→    def write_best_effort(self, data: dict, *, context: str) -> OutputResult:
    25→        result = self.write(data)
    26→        if not result.ok:
    27→            detail = result.message or "unknown write failure"
    28→            print(
    29→                colorize(
    30→                    f"  Warning: {context} succeeded but query artifact was not written ({detail}).",
    31→                    "yellow",
    32→                ),
    33→                file=sys.stderr,
    34→            )
    35→        return result
    36→
    37→
    38→def query_writer() -> QueryWriter:
    39→    """Construct a writer bound to the active runtime query path."""
    40→    return QueryWriter(query_file=query_file_path())

    44→    """Write structured query output using default best-effort policy."""

    48→def write_query_best_effort(data: dict, *, context: str) -> OutputResult:

     9→def plan_aware_queue_count(state: dict, plan: dict | None = None) -> int:
    10→    """Count remaining plan-aware queue items (skips excluded, clusters collapsed)."""

    25→
    26→def get_plan_start_strict(plan: dict | None) -> float | None:
    27→    """Extract the frozen plan-start strict score, or None if unset."""
    28→    if not plan:
    29→        return None
    30→    return plan.get("plan_start_scores", {}).get("strict")
    31→
    32→
    33→def print_frozen_score_with_queue_context(
    34→    plan: dict,
    35→    queue_remaining: int,
    36→) -> None:
    37→    """Show frozen plan-start score + queue progress."""
    38→    scores = plan.get("plan_start_scores", {})
    39→    strict = scores.get("strict")
    40→    if strict is None:
    41→        return
    42→    print(
    43→        colorize(
    44→            f"\n  Score (frozen at plan start): strict {strict:.1f}/100",
    45→            "cyan",
    46→        )
    47→    )
    48→    print(
    49→        colorize(
    50→            f"  Queue: {queue_remaining} item{'s' if queue_remaining != 1 else ''}"
    51→            " remaining. Score will not update until the queue is clear and you run `desloppify scan`.",
    52→            "dim",
    53→        )
    54→    )
    55→
    56→
    57→def print_execution_or_reveal(
    58→    state: dict,
    59→    prev,
    60→    plan: dict | None,
    61→) -> None:
    62→    """Context-aware score display: frozen plan-start score or live scores.
    63→
    64→    If a plan has ``plan_start_scores`` and there are queue items remaining,
    65→    show the frozen score + queue progress.  Otherwise delegate to the
    66→    existing live ``print_score_update``.
    67→    """
    68→    if plan and plan.get("plan_start_scores", {}).get("strict") is not None:
    69→        try:
    70→            remaining = plan_aware_queue_count(state, plan)
    71→        except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
    72→            remaining = 0
    73→        if remaining > 0:
    74→            print_frozen_score_with_queue_context(plan, remaining)
    75→            return
    76→
    77→    # No active plan cycle or queue is clear — live scores
    78→    from desloppify.app.commands.helpers.score_update import print_score_update
    79→
    80→    print_score_update(state, prev)
    81→
    82→
    83→def show_score_with_plan_context(state: dict, prev) -> None:

    86→    Encapsulates the common load_plan + PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS + reveal
    87→    choreography so command modules don't each repeat it.
    88→    """
    89→    from desloppify.engine.plan import load_plan
    90→
    91→    try:
    92→        plan = load_plan()
    93→    except PLAN_LOAD_EXCEPTIONS:
    94→        plan = None
    95→    print_execution_or_reveal(state, prev, plan)

   165→        for names in file_names_map.values():

   141→        if isinstance(file_path, str) and file_path.strip()
   142→    }
   143→    reviewed_files_abs = {
   144→        _absolutize_review_path(file_path, project_root=resolved_project_root)
   145→        for file_path in reviewed_files_rel
   146→    }
   147→    review_potential_files = valid_reviewed_files | {
   148→        *reviewed_files_rel,
   149→        *reviewed_files_abs,
   150→    }
   151→
   152→    potentials = _lang_potentials(state, lang_name)
   153→    potentials["review"] = len(review_potential_files)
   154→
   155→    diff = merge_scan(
   156→        state,
   157→        review_findings,
   158→        options=MergeScanOptions(
   159→            lang=lang_name,
   160→            potentials={"review": potentials.get("review", 0)},
   161→            merge_potentials=True,
   162→        ),
   163→    )
   164→
   165→    new_ids = {finding["id"] for finding in review_findings}
   166→    reimported_files = valid_reviewed_files
   167→    auto_resolve_review_findings(
   168→        state,
   169→        new_ids=new_ids,
   170→        diff=diff,
   171→        note="not reported in latest per-file re-import",
   172→        should_resolve=lambda finding: (
   173→            finding.get("detector") == "review"
   174→            and not finding.get("detail", {}).get("holistic")
   175→            and finding.get("file", "") in reimported_files
   176→        ),
   177→        utc_now_fn=utc_now_fn,
   178→    )
   179→
   180→    if skipped:
   181→        diff["skipped"] = len(skipped)
   182→        diff["skipped_details"] = skipped
   183→
   184→    update_review_cache(
   185→        state,
   186→        findings_list,
   187→        reviewed_files=reviewed_files,
   188→        project_root=resolved_project_root,
   189→        utc_now_fn=utc_now_fn,
   190→    )
   191→    return diff
   192→
   193→
   194→def update_review_cache(
   195→    state: dict[str, Any],
   196→    findings_data: list[ReviewFindingPayload],
   197→    *,
   198→    reviewed_files: list[str] | None = None,
   199→    project_root: Path | str | None = None,
   200→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,
   201→) -> None:
   202→    """Update per-file review cache with timestamps and content hashes."""
   203→    findings_by_file: dict[str, int] = {}
   204→    for finding in findings_data:
   205→        file_path = finding.get("file")
   206→        if not isinstance(file_path, str):
   207→            continue
   208→        findings_by_file[file_path] = findings_by_file.get(file_path, 0) + 1
   209→
   210→    refresh_review_file_cache(
   211→        state,
   212→        reviewed_files=reviewed_files,
   213→        findings_by_file=findings_by_file,
   214→        project_root=project_root,
   215→        hash_file_fn=hash_file,
   216→        utc_now_fn=utc_now_fn,
   217→    )
   218→

> DEVELOPER

You are a blind code quality reviewer for a Python codebase at /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify.

Your job: review 5 dimensions of code quality and write a JSON file with assessments and findings.

## Your Dimensions

1. **test_strategy**: Untested critical paths, coupling, snapshot overuse, fragility patterns
   - Look for: critical untested code paths (state mutations, I/O boundaries), test coupling to implementation, brittle test assertions, missing edge case coverage, test files with no assertions
   - Skip: reasonable test helper utilities, standard framework test patterns

2. **api_surface_coherence**: Inconsistent API shapes, mixed sync/async, overloaded interfaces
   - Look for: inconsistent return types across sibling functions, mixed sync/async in same module, overloaded interfaces with many optional params, public API that exposes internals
   - Skip: framework-required API shapes, versioned API compatibility

3. **authorization_consistency**: Auth/permission patterns consistently applied across the codebase
   - Look for: auth gaps in sibling routes, service role usage, RLS coverage, inconsistent permission checks
   - Skip: public endpoints, internal-only services, development-mode shortcuts

4. **dependency_health**: Unused deps, version conflicts, multiple libs for same purpose, heavy deps
   - Look for: unused packages in requirements, multiple libraries for same purpose, pinned versions with known vulnerabilities, heavy deps for light usage
   - Skip: dev/test dependencies, standard library usage, framework core deps

5. **incomplete_migration**: Old+new API coexistence, deprecated-but-called symbols, stale migration shims
   - Look for: deprecated markers still used, old API alongside new API, TODO comments about migration, backwards-compat shims, dual code paths
   - Skip: intentional backwards compatibility, versioned APIs, gradual rollout patterns

## Review Method

1. Read /tmp/review_group_strategy.json first - it has key files and batch hints
2. Explore the codebase freely. Check tests/, requirements, configuration files, etc.
3. Score each dimension 0-100 (start at 100, subtract for evidenced issues)
4. Report specific defect findings

## Scoring Anchors
- 100: exemplary. 90: strong, minor issues. 80: solid, repeated minor or one moderate. 70: mixed. 60: significant drag. 40: poor.
- Scores below 85 MUST have at least one finding for that dimension
- Score from evidence, not targets.

## Output Format

Write a JSON file to /tmp/review_result_strategy.json:
```json
{
  "assessments": {
    "test_strategy": 75.0,
    "api_surface_coherence": 80.0,
    ...
  },
  "findings": [
    {
      "dimension": "test_strategy",
      "identifier": "short_id",
      "summary": "One-line (< 120 chars)",
      "related_files": ["relative/path.py"],
      "evidence": ["specific observation"],
      "suggestion": "concrete action",
      "confidence": "high|medium|low"
    }
  ]
}
```

IMPORTANT RULES:
- Findings must be DEFECTS only, never positive observations
- Every finding needs related_files and concrete suggestion
- Be specific: name actual files, functions, patterns
- Quality over volume

    10→
    11→
    12→def scorecard_dimension_rows(
    13→    state: dict,
    14→    *,
    15→    dim_scores: dict | None = None,
    16→) -> list[tuple[str, dict]]:
    17→    """Return scorecard rows using canonical dimension ordering.
    18→
    19→    Tries ``prepare_scorecard_dimensions`` from the app layer when available
    20→    (deferred import to avoid hard engine -> app dependency), then falls back
    21→    to a simple mechanical-dimension listing.
    22→    """
    23→    if dim_scores is None:
    24→        dim_scores = (
    25→            state.get("dimension_scores", {}) if isinstance(state, dict) else {}
    26→        )
    27→        projected_state = state
    28→    else:
    29→        projected_state = dict(state)
    30→        projected_state["dimension_scores"] = dim_scores
    31→
    32→    # Try the full app-layer scorecard projection when it can be imported.
    33→    try:
    34→        from desloppify.app.output.scorecard_parts.dimensions import (
    35→            prepare_scorecard_dimensions,
    36→        )
    37→
    38→        rows = prepare_scorecard_dimensions(projected_state)
    39→        if rows:
    40→            return rows
    41→    except ImportError as exc:
    42→        _ = exc
    43→
    44→    # Fallback for synthetic/unit-test states without full scorecard context.
    45→    fallback_dim_scores = dim_scores or {}
    46→    if not isinstance(fallback_dim_scores, dict):
    47→        return []
    48→
    49→    mechanical_names = [dimension.name for dimension in DIMENSIONS]
    50→    fallback_rows: list[tuple[str, dict]] = []
    51→    for name in mechanical_names:
    52→        data = fallback_dim_scores.get(name)
    53→        if isinstance(data, dict):
    54→            fallback_rows.append((name, data))
    55→    fallback_rows.extend(
    56→        sorted(
    57→            [
    58→                (name, data)
    59→                for name, data in fallback_dim_scores.items()
    60→                if name not in mechanical_names and isinstance(data, dict)
    61→            ],
    62→            key=lambda item: item[0].lower(),
    63→        )
    64→    )
    65→    return fallback_rows
    66→

1→"""Pure mutation operations on the plan model."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.engine._plan.schema import (
     6→    Cluster,
     7→    PlanModel,
     8→    SkipEntry,
     9→    empty_plan,
    10→    ensure_plan_defaults,
    11→)
    12→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import utc_now
    13→
    14→
    15→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    16→# Helpers
    17→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    18→
    19→def _remove_id_from_lists(plan: PlanModel, finding_id: str) -> None:
    20→    """Remove a finding ID from queue_order and skipped."""
    21→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
    22→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan.get("skipped", {})
    23→    if finding_id in order:
    24→        order.remove(finding_id)
    25→    skipped.pop(finding_id, None)
    26→
    27→
    28→def _resolve_position(
    29→    order: list[str],
    30→    position: str,
    31→    target: str | None = None,
    32→    offset: int | None = None,
    33→    finding_ids: list[str] | None = None,
    34→) -> int:
    35→    """Resolve a position specifier to an insertion index.
    36→
    37→    *finding_ids* are the IDs being moved — used to calculate relative
    38→    positions when they already exist in the list.
    39→    """
    40→    moving = set(finding_ids or [])
    41→
    42→    if position == "top":
    43→        return 0
    44→    if position == "bottom":
    45→        return len(order)
    46→
    47→    if position in {"before", "after"} and target:
    48→        return _resolve_relative_position(order, moving, position=position, target=target)
    49→
    50→    if position in {"up", "down"} and offset is not None:
    51→        return _resolve_offset_position(
    52→            order,
    53→            moving,
    54→            position=position,
    55→            offset=offset,
    56→            finding_ids=finding_ids,
    57→        )
    58→
    59→    return len(order)
    60→
    61→
    62→def _resolve_relative_position(
    63→    order: list[str],
    64→    moving: set[str],
    65→    *,
    66→    position: str,
    67→    target: str,
    68→) -> int:
    69→    for i, item_id in enumerate(order):
    70→        if item_id == target and item_id not in moving:
    71→            return i if position == "before" else i + 1
    72→    return 0 if position == "before" else len(order)
    73→
    74→
    75→def _find_index(items: list[str], target: str) -> int | None:
    76→    for i, item_id in enumerate(items):
    77→        if item_id == target:
    78→            return i
    79→    return None
    80→
    81→
    82→def _resolve_offset_position(
    83→    order: list[str],
    84→    moving: set[str],
    85→    *,
    86→    position: str,
    87→    offset: int,
    88→    finding_ids: list[str] | None,
    89→) -> int:
    90→    if not finding_ids:
    91→        return 0 if position == "up" else len(order)
    92→    first_id = finding_ids[0]
    93→    clean_order = [x for x in order if x not in moving]
    94→    current_idx = _find_index(clean_order, first_id)
    95→    if current_idx is None:
    96→        if position == "up":
    97→            return max(0, len(clean_order) - offset)
    98→        return len(clean_order)
    99→    if position == "up":
   100→        return max(0, current_idx - offset)
   101→    return min(len(clean_order), current_idx + offset)
   102→
   103→
   104→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   105→# Move items
   106→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   107→
   108→def move_items(
   109→    plan: PlanModel,
   110→    finding_ids: list[str],
   111→    position: str,
   112→    target: str | None = None,
   113→    offset: int | None = None,
   114→) -> int:
   115→    """Move finding IDs to a position in queue_order. Returns count moved."""
   116→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   117→    order: list[str] = plan["queue_order"]
   118→
   119→    # Remove from skipped if present
   120→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan.get("skipped", {})
   121→    for fid in finding_ids:
   122→        skipped.pop(fid, None)
   123→
   124→    # Remove from current position in order
   125→    for fid in finding_ids:
   126→        if fid in order:
   127→            order.remove(fid)
   128→
   129→    # Resolve insertion point
   130→    idx = _resolve_position(order, position, target, offset, finding_ids)
   131→
   132→    # Insert in original order
   133→    for i, fid in enumerate(finding_ids):
   134→        order.insert(idx + i, fid)
   135→
   136→    return len(finding_ids)
   137→
   138→
   139→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   140→# Skip / unskip
   141→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   142→
   143→def skip_items(
   144→    plan: PlanModel,
   145→    finding_ids: list[str],
   146→    *,
   147→    kind: str = "temporary",
   148→    reason: str | None = None,
   149→    note: str | None = None,
   150→    attestation: str | None = None,
   151→    review_after: int | None = None,
   152→    scan_count: int = 0,
   153→) -> int:
   154→    """Move finding IDs to the skipped dict. Returns count skipped."""
   155→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   156→    now = utc_now()
   157→    count = 0
   158→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan["skipped"]
   159→    for fid in finding_ids:
   160→        _remove_id_from_lists(plan, fid)
   161→        skipped[fid] = {
   162→            "finding_id": fid,
   163→            "kind": kind,
   164→            "reason": reason,
   165→            "note": note,
   166→            "attestation": attestation,
   167→            "created_at": now,
   168→            "review_after": review_after,
   169→            "skipped_at_scan": scan_count,
   170→        }
   171→        count += 1
   172→    return count
   173→
   174→
   175→def unskip_items(
   176→    plan: PlanModel, finding_ids: list[str]
   177→) -> tuple[int, list[str]]:
   178→    """Bring finding IDs back from skipped to the end of queue_order.
   179→
   180→    Returns ``(count_unskipped, permanent_ids_needing_state_reopen)``
   181→    where the second list contains IDs that were permanent or false_positive
   182→    and need their state-layer status reopened by the caller.
   183→    """
   184→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   185→    count = 0
   186→    need_reopen: list[str] = []
   187→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan["skipped"]
   188→    for fid in finding_ids:
   189→        entry = skipped.pop(fid, None)
   190→        if entry is not None:
   191→            if entry.get("kind") in ("permanent", "false_positive"):
   192→                need_reopen.append(fid)
   193→            if fid not in plan["queue_order"]:
   194→                plan["queue_order"].append(fid)
   195→            count += 1
   196→    return count, need_reopen
   197→
   198→
   199→def resurface_stale_skips(
   200→    plan: PlanModel, current_scan_count: int
   201→) -> list[str]:
   202→    """Move temporary skips past their review_after threshold back to queue.
   203→
   204→    Returns list of resurfaced finding IDs.
   205→    """
   206→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   207→    skipped: dict[str, SkipEntry] = plan["skipped"]
   208→    resurfaced: list[str] = []
   209→    for fid in list(skipped):
   210→        entry = skipped[fid]
   211→        if entry.get("kind") != "temporary":
   212→            continue
   213→        review_after = entry.get("review_after")
   214→        if review_after is None:
   215→            continue
   216→        skipped_at = entry.get("skipped_at_scan", 0)
   217→        if current_scan_count >= skipped_at + review_after:
   218→            skipped.pop(fid)
   219→            if fid not in plan["queue_order"]:
   220→                plan["queue_order"].append(fid)
   221→            resurfaced.append(fid)
   222→    return resurfaced
   223→

   229→def describe_finding(

   232→    """Set or clear an augmented description on a finding."""
   233→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   234→    now = utc_now()
   235→    overrides = plan["overrides"]
   236→    if finding_id not in overrides:
   237→        overrides[finding_id] = {"finding_id": finding_id, "created_at": now}
   238→    overrides[finding_id]["description"] = description
   239→    overrides[finding_id]["updated_at"] = now
   240→
   241→
   242→def annotate_finding(
